change.summary: Competent authorities must assess and follow up on substantiated concerns about non-compliance within 30 days, protect the identity of reporters, and allow affected persons to challenge authority decisions. These articles set out rights and duties for operators and traders under the Regulation.

obligations.text: Inform submitters of follow-up within 30 days of receiving a substantiated concern.
obligations.quote: Within 30 days of receiving a substantiated concern, if not otherwise stated in national law, the competent authority shall inform the persons referred to in paragraph 1, who submitted the substantiated concerns, of the follow-up given to the submission and shall provide the reasons for it.

obligations.text: Competent authorities shall assess substantiated concerns diligently and impartially.
obligations.quote: Competent authorities shall, without undue delay, diligently and impartially assess the substantiated concerns, including whether the claims are well-founded, and take the necessary steps, including carrying out checks and conducting hearings of operators, downstream operators and traders, with a view to detecting potential non-compliance with this Regulation and, where appropriate, taking interim measures under Article 23 to prevent the placing or making available on the market and export of relevant products under investigation.

obligations.text: Provide for measures to protect the identity of persons who submit substantiated concerns.
obligations.quote: Member States shall provide for measures to protect the identity of the natural or legal persons who submit substantiated concerns or who conduct investigations with the aim of verifying compliance by operators, downstream operators or traders with this Regulation.

obligations.text: Have access to administrative or judicial procedures to review the legality of authority decisions.
obligations.quote: Any natural or legal person having a sufficient interest, as determined in accordance with the existing national systems of legal remedies, including where such persons meet the criteria, if any, laid down in the national law, including persons who have submitted a substantiated concern in accordance with Article 31, shall have access to administrative or judicial procedures to review the legality of the decisions, acts or failure to act of the competent authorities under this Regulation.

reasons: The four obligations you were given are all addressed to competent authorities or Member States — they require authorities to inform submitters, assess concerns, protect reporters' identities, and give persons access to review procedures.

Your shop is an operator/trader that sells furniture and leather goods to several EU countries, but these articles impose no duties on sellers; they only govern how authorities handle substantiated concerns about non-compliance.
